title: Sri Lanka staring down the barrel of defeat | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 19 November 2026 05:10
-     - 2

RAWALPINDI: Pakistan maintained their stranglehold in the second cricket Test against Sri Lanka gaining a first innings lead of 227 and then reducing their opponents to 74-3 in the second innings by stumps on the second day at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium here yesterday.

Sri Lanka trail Pakistan by 153 runs with seven second innings wickets in hand and face a long haul with three more days of the Test remaining.

Pakistan resumed day two at 121-3 and lost Azan Awais early, but the middle and lower-order fought hard. Ghazi Ghori top-scored with a maiden half-century – 54 off 90 balls (4 fours) while there were useful contributions from Saqib Khan (37) and Razuallah (42 off 32 balls, 4 fours, 3 sixes).

Pakistan were eventually bowled out for 325 on the stroke of tea, gaining an overall lead of 227 runs. They then put Sri Lanka in early trouble once again. Saqib Khan dismissed Lahiru Udara early and the woefully out-of-form Dinesh Chandimal was trapped in front by Razaullah for a duck. Kamindu Mendis once again pushed hard at a wide ball, edging it to slip to make Sri Lanka 39-3.

Dhananjaya de Silva played some sublime shots and looked in good touch finishing the day on 24* while Pasindu Sooriyabandara had looked patient for his 18* off 61 balls.

Pakistan’s innings had two halves. Azan Awais (47 off 104) and Tayyab Arif (46 off 82) gave them a solid platform, and nightwatchman Saqib Khan dug in for a gutsy 37 off 78. Lahiru Kumara then ripped through the middle order and bowled his heart out. Babar Azam fell for 8 to Kumara, Mohammad Taha made 8, Saud Shakeel 24 and Salman Ali Agha 21, and Pakistan were 221-7 at lunch. But Ghazi Ghori had other ideas and thrived under pressure. He shepherded the tail superbly, and his 54 helped the last three wickets add 104 after the break. Every run he scraped together was a body blow for a Sri Lankan side already bogged down after being skittled for 98. Kumara was the pick of the bowlers with his second five-wicket haul, and Asitha Fernando took three.

title: Depleted India stamp their class to retain SAFF crown | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 19 November 2026 05:09
-     - 1

Team India celebrating their stunning victory

By Althaf Nawaz

Missing several senior players, India went into the final with a squad of just 17, yet stamped their class to stay on top of South Asian football.

A spirited second-half rally enabled defending champions India to overcome traditional rivals Pakistan 2-1 and retain the prestigious SAFF Championship for a record 10th occasion in a pulsating final of the 15th SAFF Football Tournament, played under lights at the National Stadium in Dhaka, Bangladesh, last Tuesday.

Before a vociferous crowd of over 10,000 spectators, the two traditional rivals produced a fiercely contested encounter that kept the fans on the edge of their seats. Following the elimination of hosts Bangladesh by Pakistan in the semi-finals, the final turned out to be a keenly balanced contest, with both sides determined to wrest the crown.

Pakistan started on the front foot, displaying attacking intent and putting the Indian defence under pressure. Their persistence paid dividends in first-half stoppage time when they broke the deadlock to take a slender lead into half-time.

However, after the break, India returned with renewed determination and tactical discipline. Despite fielding a depleted squad of just 17 players, with several senior players away on tour in New Zealand, the defending champions raised their game considerably in the second half.

The Indian outfit stepped up the tempo, pressed high and mounted sustained pressure on the Pakistan defence. The momentum shifted decisively in India’s favour midway through the second half when Pakistan’s Junaid Mohammed Shah was shown a straight red card, leaving his side to continue with ten men.

Capitalising on their numerical advantage, India seized control of the proceedings and intensified their attacking moves. Their relentless pressure eventually paid dividends as they found the back of the net twice to turn the deficit into a memorable 2-1 victory and successfully defend their crown.

The triumph further consolidated India’s supremacy in South Asian football, as they extended their remarkable record to 10 SAFF Championship titles, reaffirming their status as the region’s dominant force.

Pakistan had to settle for the runner-up position after a spirited campaign, while hosts Bangladesh, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and the Maldives occupied the remaining positions in the final standings.

India’s triumph was a fitting climax to the 15th edition of the SAFF Championship, with the traditional rivalry between India and Pakistan providing a thrilling finale to the regional football extravaganza.

title: Duckett ton and impressive bowlers give England series win | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 19 November 2026 05:04
-     - 1

England confidently swept aside Australia in the third one-day international in Hobart to seal a statement series win.

At times the series decider felt inconsequential - the latest seismic turn in Australia’s sandpaper scandal taking all attention during Australia’s chase - but Harry Brook’s side won by 97 runs in an important step as they build towards next year’s World Cup.

Even when failing to fully take advantage of a fast start, England reached 328 before being bowled out in the penultimate over, with Ben Duckett making a fine 133 from 115 balls.

Duckett’s century, after all of his struggles in last winter’s Ashes, was his first for England on Australian soil. A 48-ball 59 from Will Jacks ensured his innings was not wasted as Australia’s spinners slowed scoring through the middle.

Just as impressive was another exciting effort from England’s new-ball pair Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker.

Atkinson dismissed Travis Head for the third time in a row in the first over - something to be noted before next year’s Ashes series. He also hit Cameron Green with a brutal bouncer that forced the all-rounder to retire hurt.

Baker had Australia Captain Mitchell Marsh caught at second slip in the second over, soon added the wicket of Josh Inglis and also dismissed Green’s concussion replacement Oliver Peake en route to figures of 4-45.

It helped England calmly close out the win and, after being dismissed for 131 in the series opener, their recovery is noteworthy.

Australia, meanwhile, have questions to ponder on and off the field - many of which are unlikely to be answered before a five-match T20 series begins between these sides on Saturday.

Scores:

England 328 (48.3 overs) (Duckett 133, Jacks 59; Edwards 4-31) beat Australia 231 (46.5 overs) (Renshaw 55; Baker 4-45) by 97 runs.

title: Back-to-back champions: Link Natural Products retains Cup at 54th Mercantile Rugby 7s | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 19 November 2026 04:55
-     - 0

Strength, speed and teamwork carry Link Natural to a second consecutive Cup title, a reflection of the same spirit that drives the organisation’s commitment to excellence

Link Natural Products Ltd., home to the iconic Samahan brand, has built a strong reputation in Sri Lanka and international markets through its commitment to quality, innovation and excellence. This same spirit of dedication, teamwork and perseverance was reflected on the rugby field, as the company’s team secured its second consecutive Cup title at the Mercantile Rugby 7s.

Link Natural Products has once again been crowned Cup Champions of the Mercantile Rugby 7s, retaining its title at the 54th edition of the tournament held on 13 and 14 November, 2026 at the CR&FC Grounds, Longden Place, Colombo. Link Natural defeated John Keells Holdings PLC 28-17 in a hard-fought Cup final, completing back-to-back victories following its title-winning debut at the 53rd Mercantile Rugby 7s in 2025.

Organised by the Mercantile Rugby Football Association (MRFA), the Mercantile 7s is one of Sri Lanka’s oldest sporting traditions. First played in 1966, it has brought the country’s corporate sector together on the rugby field for six decades. Winning it once is an achievement; defending the title against the best of Sri Lanka’s mercantile sector is a statement of consistency.

The team’s performance brought together individual skill, discipline, fitness and a shared determination to see the job through.

“Retaining this title is a proud moment for the entire Link Natural family. It reflects the same values we live by every day: preparation, teamwork and the determination to deliver our best. We congratulate our players, coaches and everyone who supported the team,” Link Natural Products CEO Ashan Ransilige said.

With a second consecutive Mercantile Rugby 7s title, Link Natural looks ahead with the same confidence it carries onto the field. Backed by a strong foundation, a dedicated team and a forward-looking vision, the organisation remains committed to reaching new milestones in sport, in business and in the lives of the people it serves.

This victory is a reminder that lasting success is built through consistent performance, strong partnerships and an unwavering commitment to excellence.

title: Brazil defeat Singapore 7-0 as Vinicius scores first-half hat-trick | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 19 November 2026 04:25
-     - 2

Vinicius Junior celebrates scoring their second goal against Singapore in Brazil’s 7-0 win in the international friendly football match

Vinicius Junior hit a 12-minute hat-trick in the first half as Brazil turned on the style in a 7-0 trouncing of Singapore in an international friendly.

Endrick, Estevao, Rayan and substitute Allan also found the net as the South Americans brushed aside their hosts with a dominant performance at the National Stadium on Tuesday.

Brazil were much changed from their 3-2 loss to Japan on Saturday, in which manager Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were shown red cards, with Vinicius one of only four players retaining their places in the starting lineup.

Bruno Guimaraes took over as skipper and set up the opener after nine minutes, playing a quick pass to Vinicius, who wrong-footed Singapore captain Hariss Harun with his first touch before dispatching a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Izwan Mahbud.

The Real Madrid forward notched his second in the 15th minute after a quick counterattack by the Selecao as Endrick laid the ball off for his unmarked teammate to slot home.

Vinicius was denied by Izwan shortly afterwards, but he completed his hat-trick in the 21st minute when he was found completely unmarked in the six-yard box by Estevao’s low centre. Rayan had an effort disallowed for offside, but Endrick added to Brazil’s lead in the 31st minute with a low effort from range that found the bottom right corner.

Estevao also had a goal disallowed for a foul by Vinicius, but the Chelsea winger added to Brazil’s tally just after the interval with a deflected shot from the edge of the box.

Rayan rocked the crossbar soon after, but the endeavour of the Bournemouth forward was rewarded in the 65th minute when he rounded substitute goalkeeper Syazwan Buhari to make it 6-0.

Brazil rang the changes in the closing stages, and Allan came off the bench to grab the seventh goal in the 74th minute with a low-angled shot that nicked off Raoul Suhaimi on its way into the net.

title: NEGC Club Championship to light up Hill Country | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 19 November 2026 04:14
-     - 6

By Shamseer Jaleel

The Nuwara Eliya Golf Club (NEGC) Club Championship 2026 will once again celebrate the rich golfing heritage of the Hill Country, teeing off on 28 November. The Club Championship will continue on Day 2 as well. Meanwhile, the Sinclair Cup will take place on 27 November.

Maj. Gen. (Retd.) Srinath Rajapakse and Sachin De Silva will defend their titles. Rajapakse will defend his Nett Championship title, while De Silva returns as the defending Gross Champion. The Annual Gold Medal was won by Jevahn Sathasivam. In the ladies’ segment, the Captain’s Cup will be defended by youngster Kaitylyn Norton, while Kayla Perera will defend her Club Championship title in Nuwara Eliya.

The NEGC Club Championship boasts a proud history dating back to 1933, when M.H. Lushington became its inaugural men’s champion. The Nuwara Eliya Golf Club itself, established in 1889, is one of Asia’s oldest golf clubs.

With its historic 18-hole course, surrounded by towering trees and the picturesque tea-country landscape, the NEGC remains one of Sri Lanka’s most treasured golfing destinations, preserving a remarkable tradition spanning generations. More than 75 golfers have already registered for these annual events.

title: SLT-Mobitel powers Sri Lankan Netball | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 19 November 2026 04:11
-     - 6

Mobitel COO Sudharshana Geeganage (second from left) presents the sponsorship cheque to Netball Federation of Sri Lanka President Vajira Janaki Nethicumara, accompanied by (from left) Mobitel Senior General Manager Marketing Isuru Dissanayake and Netball Federation of Sri Lanka Treasurer B. D. Sumithra

Reaffirming its commitment to empowering sports, SLT-Mobitel, the National ICT Solutions Provider, has partnered with the Netball Federation of Sri Lanka (NFSL) as the main sponsor for the 2026 Junior and Senior National Netball Championships, the sport’s two flagship national tournaments, taking place at Torrington Grounds. The sponsorship highlights SLT-MOBITEL’s focus on national pride, social progress, connectivity, and support for sport in Sri Lanka.

As the pinnacle of domestic netball, the annual championships bring together elite talent from across 25 District Netball Associations. SLT-Mobitel takes pride in powering this prestigious platform, providing the nation’s top athletes with the opportunity to showcase their skill and determination. Through this partnership, SLT-Mobitel remains deeply committed to supporting grassroots development, nurturing emerging talent and championing the growth of women’s sports across Sri Lanka.

Netball has been played in Sri Lanka for over a century and is part of the national school curriculum. Furthermore, its low and affordable infrastructure requirements have made it a deeply rooted and accessible sport across the country. Its widespread popularity, combined with Sri Lanka’s consistent success on the international stage, has inspired many young women, particularly from rural communities, to take up the sport.

Driving female empowerment and inclusivity for these athletes, netball is more than a game. It is a vital pathway to enhancing social mobility and economic status. NFSL’s aim is to develop the country’s raw talent, offering players platforms to showcase their skills, and create spaces for women to demonstrate their athletic talent. The sponsorship also supports the NFSL’s strategic roadmap to elevate the standards of netball and reclaim Sri Lanka’s status as a powerhouse in Asia, with a focus on elite youth development. The Junior Nationals, scheduled from 21 to 22 November 2026, also serves as a scouting ground to select players for the youth national pool. 

With a shared focus on national pride and youth development, SLT-Mobitel’s backing ensures that the next wave of Sri Lankan netball stars has the support needed to thrive.

The championship provided a competitive platform for school children from across the country to showcase their skills, determination and sportsmanship while gaining valuable experience through high-level inter-school competition.

In the U20 Boys’ Division A – Tier I, St. Joseph’s College, Colombo, emerged as champions, while Ananda College, Colombo, secured the first runner-up position. Royal College, Colombo, and Trinity College, Kandy, finished as the second and third runners-up, respectively.

In the U20 Girls’ Division A – Tier I, Holy Family Convent, Colombo, clinched the championship, while St. Joseph’s College, Nugegoda, was named first runner-up. St. Bridget’s Convent, Colombo, and Mahamaya Girls’ College, Kandy, secured the second and third runner-up positions, respectively.

The tournament featured several categories across the U20 Boys’ and Girls’ divisions, with schools from different parts of Sri Lanka recording notable performances.
